reason: The cited evidence shows HEAs can have good oxidation/corrosion resistance (E4, E7, E9) and that oxide films can affect friction (E8), but none of the passages demonstrate that a stable, dense oxide layer governs the coupled tribo-corrosion response by simultaneously reducing wear and corrosion through barrier and friction-lowering mechanisms. The specific claims about oxide layers governing the coupled response, reducing friction, and improving mechanical properties are not directly supported by the cited studies.
premises: HEAs can form stable, dense oxide layers that act as protective barriers
Oxide layers reduce further oxidation and corrosion by blocking corrosive species
Oxide layers reduce wear by lowering the coefficient of friction
Tribo-corrosion response is governed primarily by oxide layer formation rather than alloy composition or microstructure
Oxide layer formation improves mechanical properties and thermal stability
